title: A quantitative nearby root from coefficient proximity
statement:
Let $L/K$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] of normed fields, with the norm of $L$ extending the norm of $K$. A normed field here means a field with a real-valued norm satisfying $\|z\|\geq0$, $\|z\|=0\Leftrightarrow z=0$, $\|1\|=1$, $\|zw\|=\|z\|\|w\|$ and $\|z+w\|\leq\|z\|+\|w\|$, with distance $d(z,w)=\|z-w\|$. Let $f,g\in K[T]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] be monic of the same degree $n\geq1$. Let $x\in L$ satisfy $f(x)=0$, with evaluation as in [def-weil-polynomial-root]. Assume $g$ splits in $L[T]$, meaning it is a product of $n$ linear factors there. If $\varepsilon>0$ and $\|g_i-f_i\|<\varepsilon$ for every $i\geq0$, then there is $b\in L$ with $g(b)=0$ and
$$\|x-b\|<\big((n+1)\varepsilon\big)^{1/n}\max\{\|x\|,1\}.$$
